title: Question
description: Derived from ISSUE_FORMAT.md 0.7; the document wins. One question as stored (section 5.1), with the ids and round that software adds.
$comment: Derived from ISSUE_FORMAT.md 0.7; the document wins. Not expressed here: that every tagged issue exists and may be asked (5.1 rule 2), the standard closing options (5.1, Options item 2), the grouped rate-law question (5.1 rule 3), which options of a question are rate-law options (that needs the tagged issues), whether a rate-law option passes the checks of 3.1 (Rate-law bindings), and the plain-language rule (5.3). The shape of a rate-law option's value, with the proposed key names of design/HANDOFFS.md 2.9, is $defs/rate_law_option_value, for the question-round file to use. In design/HANDOFFS.md 2.9 the closing options and the grouping are content checks. 5.1 itself fixes no value for the closing options; design/HANDOFFS.md 2.9 fixes the values free_entry ("A different value") and does_not_fit ("The question does not fit"), as in the example, which comes from Issue format 10.1. That is a design rule (not part of Issue format), and this file does not express it.

question_id.description: Written by software. Q-001 and so on.

round.description: Written by software. The round of the question.

issue_ids.description: Written by the inquiry agent. Hidden tags; at least one. The fields follow from the issues.

text.description: Written by the inquiry agent. Plain language (Issue format 5.3): no pointers, ids or EnzymeML field names.

answer_type.description: Written by the inquiry agent. value: free entry (a number with unit, text, or a list). choose_one: a choice among the options.

options.description: Written by the inquiry agent; required for choose_one. List of {label, value}.

issue_id.description: An issue id: ISS-001 and so on (Issue format 4). Written by software, never by an agent.

question_id.description: A question id: Q-001 and so on (Issue format 5.1). Written by software.

value.description: The value the option stands for; any JSON value.

object_id.description: An EnzymeML object id: a letter, then at most 127 letters, digits or underscores, matching the whole string (design/HANDOFFS.md 2.1, rows EnzymeML object ids and Whole-string grammars).

rate_law_option_value.description: The value of a fully bound rate-law option (Issue format 5.1, rule 3; 3.1, Rate-law bindings), with the proposed key names of design/HANDOFFS.md 2.9: the model, the target reaction, the measurement whose context applies, and the ids bound to each argument and species variable. The label shows names, never these ids (5.3).

model.description: Proposed name. The model's name from the starter list.

parameters.description: Proposed name. From each argument the model needs, as the starter list names it, to a parameter id.

species.description: Proposed name. From each species variable to a species id.

options_for_choose_one.$comment: Issue format 5.1: options are required for choose_one.

inquiry_agent_part.description: The fields of a question that the inquiry agent writes (Issue format 5.1, 'Written by'), before software adds question_id and round. For the question-round file of design/HANDOFFS.md 2.9.

examples.text: Both datasets give the assay pH as 7.8, but the methods text says '20mM HEPES pH 7.4'. Which pH was used in the assays?
